content.text: You’ve spent months creating your digital product—an ebook, a course, or a set of templates. You’re ready to sell. But in Kenya, Stripe and PayPal aren’t options. Local [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-solutions-zimbabwean-digital-sellers-every-detail-you-3|payment]] gateways are unreliable. Crypto is your only path, but how do you integrate it without depending on fragile platforms? This guide solves that. It’s not a workaround. It’s [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-selling-design-assets-crypto-payments-5|COREMERCH guide to infrastructure]]. You’ll own the stack. No subscriptions. No gatekeepers. Built to withstand the kind of financial isolation that turns platforms into liabilities. [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-start-selling-digital-products-crypto-honest-side-5|How to]] with GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for logic, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. By the end of this guide, you’ll deploy a system that delivers your product the moment payment hits the blockchain. No intermediaries. No platform risk. Just you, your customer, and code you control.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-11. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Start digital

Platforms fail because they’re centralized. They depend on banking systems you can’t access. This stack bypasses that. GitHub Pages hosts your storefront for free. Cloudflare Workers handle backend logic without servers. NOWPayments verifies crypto payments on-chain—no accounts required. When a customer pays, the webhook triggers instant delivery from Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. No platform touches the transaction. No single point of failure. You’re not renting infrastructure. You’re deploying it. The stack is stateless. It doesn’t store data it doesn’t need. Orders go to Supabase or Google Sheets—tools you control. The customer pays in any of 300+ cryptocurrencies. The system converts to USD at transaction time. You get paid. The product delivers. Nothing in between can break.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Start with your product files. Organize them. Name them logically. Upload to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Create a NOWPayments account—no KYC required. Choose your currencies. BSC, Solana, or TRON are recommended for fees under $0.10. Set up a GitHub or Cloudflare account for hosting. If you’re using Google Apps Script, enable the API. For Cloudflare Workers, install Wrangler. Your domain is optional but professional. Point it to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages via DNS. Write your product descriptions. Price in USD. The system will convert to crypto at checkout. Test every asset. Broken links kill sales. Compress large files. Delivery speed matters. You’re building a machine. Every part must function before you deploy.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Connect NOWPayments to your crypto wallet. Generate API keys. These will verify payments. In Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, write the webhook handler. When NOWPayments confirms a transaction, the script generates a download link. Set expiration times. One-time use links prevent piracy. For Cloudflare Workers, deploy the script via Wrangler. For Google Apps Script, trigger it via URL fetch. Test with testnet crypto. Simulate a purchase. Ensure the product delivers. Configure email notifications. Use Gmail’s SMTP for free. The customer gets a receipt. You get an order alert. Automate everything. No manual steps. The system runs itself. You focus on creating. Not fulfilling orders.
Own the infrastructure. Rent nothing.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Deploy your storefront. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Push the code. The site goes live. Share the link. Your first customer arrives. They select a product. Pay with crypto. NOWPayments verifies the transaction. The webhook fires. The script generates the download link. The customer gets their product. You get paid. Monitor the transaction in Supabase or Google Sheets. See the order. Verify the delivery. The system logs everything. No data disappears. No platform takes a cut. The first sale proves the infrastructure. Replicate it. Add more products. The stack scales with you. No upgrades required.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

With the stack deployed, scaling is systematic. Add products to your database. Update the storefront. No code changes required. Increase your NOWPayments limits. Handle higher volumes. Optimize file delivery. Use Cloudflare’s CDN for global reach. Automate marketing. Integrate email sequences via Zapier. Track conversions. Use Google Analytics or Plausible. Diversify currencies. Add stablecoins for price stability. The infrastructure adapts. You’re not scaling a platform. You’re scaling ownership. Every tool is modular. Swap components as needed. The system evolves with your business. Not the other way around.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

To sell digital products with crypto in Kenya, deploy a sovereign commerce stack. Use GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic. NOWPayments for crypto processing. Store orders in Supabase or Google Sheets. Deliver files via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. The system automates payment verification and product delivery. No platforms. No gatekeepers. Full ownership. Start with the Complete Builder Kit for blueprints and templates.
Crypto payments. Instant delivery. No platforms.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Digital creators selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, and beats often reach this infrastructure question after hitting payout restrictions or platform policy problems on Gumroad, Payhip, or Lemon Squeezy. The difference with a sovereign stack is structural: there is no platform relationship to manage, no content policy to comply with, and no payout schedule to wait on. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 deploys the complete infrastructure in 48 hours under your own accounts. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the build process for creators who prefer to self-deploy. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Organize product files. Upload to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. 2. Create a NOWPayments account. Select currencies. Generate API keys. 3. Set up GitHub or Cloudflare for hosting. Configure DNS if using a custom domain. 4. Write backend logic in Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Test the webhook. 5. Deploy the storefront. Test end-to-end. Simulate a purchase. 6. Monitor transactions in Supabase or Google Sheets. Verify deliveries. 7. Scale by adding products, optimizing delivery, and automating marketing.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’m not a developer?
Yes. The Complete Builder Kit includes templates and step-by-step guides. No coding required for basic deployment. Advanced customization may need technical skills.
What happens if a payment fails?
NOWPayments handles payment verification. If a transaction fails, the system doesn’t trigger delivery. The customer must retry. No manual intervention needed.
How do I handle refunds?
Refunds are processed manually via your crypto wallet. The system logs all transactions. You can verify purchases before issuing a refund.
Can I sell physical products with this stack?
No. This stack is designed for automated digital product delivery. Physical products require separate logistics infrastructure.
What if I want to change hosting providers?
The stack is modular. You can replace GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages with any static site host. Update the DNS. Redeploy the backend logic.
Deploy once. Scale forever. No gatekeepers.
